newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan nuclear firm raps officials for 1995 coverup.
newsitem.headline: Japan nuclear firm raps officials for 1995 coverup.

text.p: Japan's state-run nuclear power company said on Friday that it would take punitive action against 24 company officials for the cover-up of an accident which occured at one of its nuclear plants 18 months ago.
Prototype fast-breeder reactor Monju, operated by the Power Reactor and Nuclear Fuel Development Corp (PNC) on the Sea of Japan coast, was the scene of a massive sodium coolant leak in December 1995.

A PNC spokesman said that four senior company officials, including vice president Tadayoshi Suda, and 20 other company employees would be punished through a one-month suspension or a salary cut, among other measures.
The action comes after the completion of its in-house probe into the incident, the spokesman said.
PNC, which initially kept secret a videotape of the accident site, also issued a falsified report of the circumstances surrounding the event.
Thirteen days later, PNC revealed video footage which had been edited in an attempt to play down the scope of the accident.
After the cover-up was revealed, a PNC official who was questioning colleagues as part of an in-house investigation of the accident committed suicide.
Monju has remained shut since the accident.
In a related development, prosecutors asked a court on Friday to impose fines on the PNC and two of its officials over the incident.
